group: Collatz-like (phases growing by about 4/3, with a changing tail)
title: What is known about 1RB1LD_0LC1RC_1RA1RD_1LE0RB_---1LF_0LC0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_0LC1RC_1RA1RD_1LE0RB_---1LF_0LC0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Seven shift rules of the sweeps over the left zone are proved in Lean for all sizes (lean/Rules.lean). The phase structure is read off simulation. No map on numbers has been extracted yet, and the small tail at the right end changes from phase to phase.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 42,914 cells have been visited and 33,496 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.526). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.086).

claims.title: Sweeps over the left zone
claims.text: Seven shift rules: the head crosses any number of pairs of blocks 0 1^5 0 1^5, or of the 12-cell words they are re-encoded into during a visit, in states B, D, C, A, D, F, B in turn. Each rule turns one 12-cell word into another.

claims.title: One period of a phase: 6 blocks of 1^11 into 16 of 1^5
claims.text: In the middle of a phase the tape at the moment the head is in state C at the left end repeats its shape every 12 such moments: the run of 1^5 blocks has grown by 16 and the run of 1^11 blocks has shrunk by 6. bbtools.cycles proves these cycles symbolically, but the Lean files it writes are about a megabyte per rule, so they are not kept or checked.

claims.title: Phases grow by about 4/3
claims.text: A phase starts with 9 blocks of 1^5 and b blocks of 1^11 and ends with about 8b/3 blocks of 1^5, which are folded into about half as many 1^11 blocks. The starting b runs 24, 33, 53, 78, 111, 143, 196, 269, 374, 500, 661, 900, 1197, 1604, 2147, 2868, 3834, 5113 (the last at step 2,251,904,944), and the tail of a few odd blocks at the right end is different almost every time.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The halting transition is E0. E is entered only from D reading a 0 (which writes 1 and steps left), so a halt needs D to read a 0 with another 0 to its left. Whether a phase change, which depends on the tail and on residues of b, can ever produce that is open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine runs in phases: a run of long blocks 1^11 is eaten and turned into short blocks 1^5 at a fixed rate, 3 for 8; then the short blocks are folded back into long ones and a new phase starts, about 4/3 larger. Seven sweeps are proved in Lean; the phase map is not worked out yet.

facts.text: Shift rules over the left zone, proved for all sizes.
Growth from one phase to the next.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Short blocks, a gadget and long blocks
html:
Read from the left end, the tape at a typical moment is

0 0 (0 1^5)^a   [gadget]   0 1^15 (0 1^11)^b   [tail]

with a gadget of a few blocks of length 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 or 17 that cycles through 12 shapes, and a tail of a few more odd blocks. The head walks from the left end to the gadget and back again and again. On each walk it crosses the zone of short blocks several times and re-encodes it as it goes. Pairs 011111 011111 become 101011011011, then other 12-cell words, and finally the pairs again. These crossings are the seven shift rules in lean/Rules.lean.

sections.heading: Phases that grow by about four thirds
html:
Every 12 visits to the left end the gadget is back in the same shape, the short run is 16 blocks longer and the long run is 6 blocks shorter: three long blocks (36 cells) become eight short ones (48 cells). When the long run is used up, the short run is folded into about half as many long blocks and the next phase starts with 9 short blocks:

A phase costs about the square of the tape length, so one side grows like the square root of the step count. The tail at the right end is rewritten at each phase change, and so are the exact offsets: this is where the Collatz-like part sits.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The only halting transition is E on a 0. E is entered only from D reading a 0, so a halt needs 0 0 with D arriving on the right-hand 0. Inside a phase the same 12 shapes repeat, so (given the period rule, which is computed but not checked in Lean) a phase that does not halt in its first period does not halt until it ends. A halt can only come at a phase change. Settling it means working out the phase change exactly (how the tail and the residue of b mod 3 determine the next phase) and iterating that map. See the README.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.526). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.086).
After 109 steps the tape spans 42,914 cells (30,975 left of the start, 658 right), with a density of 1s of 0.781.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Three zones: a growing run of 1^5 blocks on the left, a small gadget, and a run of 1^11 blocks that is eaten 3 blocks for every 8 new 1^5 blocks; when the 1^11 run is used up the 1^5 run is folded into about half as many 1^11 blocks and a phase starts again, about 4/3 larger.
